R-performance-1 (The export loads the whole audit log and builds the CSV in memory on the event loop) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The handler runs `SELECT * FROM audit_events WHERE org_id = $1 ORDER BY
created_at`, loads the rows into an array, builds the whole CSV string with
`rows.map(toCsvLine).join("\n")`, and sends it.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: The result set grows with the organization's history: the design's own Context gives about 40 000 events per organization and per month, kept seven years, so up to about 3.4 million rows per request. All of them are held in one array, then mapped to a second array of lines, then joined into one string — memory and CPU grow linearly with the log, and the `map`/`join` runs synchronously on the single event loop ("one event loop per instance"), stalling every other request on the instance for the duration; a few concurrent exports can exhaust the heap. The spec requires every event, so keep the full export but stream it: read the rows in batches (a server-side cursor or keyset pagination on `created_at, id`), write each batch's CSV lines to the response as a stream honouring backpressure, and keep the order oldest first. Record the alternative in the decision instead of "none".
findings.title: The export loads the whole audit log and builds the CSV in memory on the event loop

findings.recommendation: The schema of `audit_events` is not in the repository, so the index could not be checked. Confirm with `EXPLAIN` that an index on `(org_id, created_at)` serves both the filter and the sort; without it the query scans the table and sorts millions of rows per export, a cost growing with every organization's data. Add the index to the plan if it is missing.
findings.title: No index is shown for the export's filter and sort
